b84330808 edited PR #15159:

This removes two methods in cranelift-entity whose unsafe code has no callers left in the workspace:

  • PrimaryMap::get_raw_mut — only referenced by its own unit test and by an equally unused wrapper in wasmtime-environ (TryPrimaryMap::get_raw_mut); both are removed. This also addresses bjorn3's point on the earlier revision: the wrapping_add there had no in-bounds guarantee to lean on, so the sound thing is for the method not to exist.
  • PrimaryMap::into_boxed_slice — only used by the BoxedSlice tests; they now construct BoxedSlice directly through its pub(crate) constructor.

Motivation: reducing the unsafe surface where the code is dead anyway. There is no bug behind this — the methods were not called, they just carried unsafe contracts for no benefit. This kind of unsafe-reduction is also the class of change covered by Google's Patch Rewards program for OSS-Fuzz projects (Tier 2 hardening), which is part of why I went looking for it.

An earlier version of this PR also added #![forbid(unsafe_code)] to the crate; I removed that again after fitzgen's review, since the crate may legitimately want unsafe in the future.

Testing: cargo test -p cranelift-entity — 59 unit tests and 2 doc tests pass; cargo check -p wasmtime-environ passes.

Open question from the review thread: BoxedSlice itself now has no users and cannot be constructed from outside the crate. I'm happy to remove it in this PR too if the maintainers want that.

b84330808 commented on PR #15159:

Fair question, and sorry for the missing context — I should have written this in the description from the start.

The motivation is honestly pretty modest. I've been looking for places where unsafe can be removed outright rather than justified, and in this crate the only two remaining pieces of unsafe turned out to be methods with no callers: get_raw_mut and PrimaryMap::into_boxed_slice. There's no bug behind it — nothing crashed and nobody hit the get_raw_mut contract in practice; it was dead code carrying an unsafe API for no benefit. For background, this kind of unsafe-reduction is also what Google's Patch Rewards program covers for OSS-Fuzz projects (Tier 2 hardening), which is part of why I went looking — but I'm not attached to landing this for that reason, and if the change isn't useful to you it shouldn't stay open just for that.

On forbid(unsafe_code): you're right, and I don't want to lock the crate against future legitimate uses of unsafe. I've pushed a commit (47f59e9) that drops the #![forbid(unsafe_code)] attribute, so what's left is only the removal of the two unused methods, which bjorn3 already reviewed above. The BoxedSlice question I asked bjorn3 in the thread is still open — happy to fold that removal in here or leave the type in place, whichever you both prefer.

If even the trimmed-down version isn't something you want, please feel free to close this — no hard feelings.

fitzgen commented on PR #15159:

@b84330808 can you clarify whether your interactions here are abiding by the project's AI policy?

b84330808 commented on PR #15159:

Yes, happy to clarify. I'm directing this work myself and I review what goes in before anything is submitted. AI tools are part of my process, but there is no unattended agent acting here — the changes, the description and these replies are mine to answer for, and I can walk through the diff if that's useful (it's a small one: two methods with no callers in the workspace, plus their tests). The missing motivation up front was my oversight; the description has it now.

I also took your point on forbid(unsafe_code) and dropped that part — the PR is just the dead-code removal at this point. If you still judge it not worth the review time, I understand closing it.

:thumbs_up: cfallin submitted PR review:

The DCE seems fine to me; this is very old code that probably was written as a generic data structure library before most of Cranelift+Wasmtime grew up around it and solidified our usage patterns.

Agreed with Nick that we don't want to forbid unsafe code; passively reducing it (if free) is always great though.

Just one nit below re: formatting. Thanks!

Locally, cargo check -p cranelift-entity --all-targets with -D warnings is clean, the tests pass (52 + 2; the seven dropped tests were BoxedSlice's own), and the crate is rustfmt-clean. Happy to restore the type if you would rather keep it.
